registry_schema.label: Design
registry_schema.text: Palliative radiation therapy is often used to improve quality of life for patients with metastatic cancer, but severe gastrointestinal (GI) toxicities can limit its effectiveness. HART (Hybrid Arc Radiation Therapy) combines dynamic conformal arcs with conventional radiation beams to deliver more precise dose distributions while sparing healthy organs. This study explores whether HART can reduce acute GI toxicities compared to traditional methods, using validated measures like PRO-CTCAE scores. The goal is to improve patient adherence, reduce side effects, and enhance quality of life, while addressing the lack of clinical data on HART's safety and effectiveness in palliative care.

registry_schema.label: Design
registry_schema.text: The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if hypofractionation of definitive chemoradiotherapy can treat patients with locally advanced esophageal cancer. The main question it aims to answer is if this treatment is feasible and safe. We also want to investigate the toxicity, in particular the radiation-induced lymphopenia. Normally, definitive chemoradiotherapy for patients with locally advanced esophageal cancer consist of 28 fractions of 1.8 Gy with concurrent 6 cycles of carboplatin and paclitaxel in 5.5 weeks. In this study, participants will receive 20 fractions of 2.4 Gy with concurrent 6 cycles of carboplatin and paclitaxel in 4 weeks. The follow-up will be conform standard-of-care.

registry_schema.label: Design
registry_schema.text: This study was conducted to explore the efficacy and toxicity of concurrent chemoradiotherapy with nab-paclitaxel, carboplatin and thoracic radiotherapy in unresectable local advanced squamous cell lung cancer. Patients will be given nab-paclitaxel weekly at a dose of 60mg/m2, in combination with carboplatin (AUC 2) weekly during concurrent chemoradiotherapy. Thoracic radiation was administered at a dose of 66 Gy/33 fractions, both 3 dimensional conformal and intensity modulated radiation therapy are allowed. Two cycles of consolidation therapy with full dose nab-paclitaxel (260 mg/m2 on day 1) and carboplatin (AUC 6 on day 1) every 21 day will be delivered.

publications.title: Icotinib With Concurrent Radiotherapy vs Radiotherapy Alone in Older Adults With Unresectable Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma: A Phase II Randomized Clinical Trial.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Randomized multicenter open-label phase II trial in older adults with unresectable esophageal squamous cell carcinoma. 127 patients were randomized, 64 to radiotherapy plus icotinib and 63 to radiotherapy.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Minimization by T stage (T2 versus T3 versus T4), N stage (N0 versus N+), and ECOG performance status (0 or 1 versus 2).

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Central 1:1 randomization. Open label. 3D conformal radiotherapy or IMRT, conventional fractionation. GTV is the primary tumor and enlarged regional nodes and is planned to 60 Gy in 30 fractions of 2 Gy. CTV adds 5 cm superiorly and inferiorly along the esophagus, 1 cm radially, and the supraclavicular and mediastinal node regions, and is planned to 40 Gy in 20 fractions of 2 Gy.

arms.text: Oral icotinib 125 mg three times daily during radiotherapy.

brief.schema_source: Trial report, Luo et al., JAMA Network Open 2020 (PMID 33026449). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Histologically confirmed unresectable or medically inoperable esophageal squamous cell carcinoma, unsuitable for concurrent chemoradiation because of comorbidity or patient choice. The printed stage line reads T2 to 24, N0/1, M0/1a by the 2002 UICC system. Stratification uses T2, T3, and T4.
Age 70 or older, ECOG performance status 2 or less, adequate renal, liver, and marrow reserve, and adequate nutrition.

Excluded: another tumor, tracheoesophageal fistula, metastatic disease, dysphagia that prevents swallowing icotinib, prior systemic treatment or thoracic radiation, or significant medical or psychiatric illness.
